papers.title: Safely Mitigating Grid Imbalance: A Hybrid Distributional Wide-Margin Recourse Approach
papers.summary: This paper proposes the Multi-Agent Distributional Wide-Margin Policy Gradient (MADWMPG) framework: a dual-policy hybrid imitation and safe reinforcement learning (IL-SRL) method designed for safely mitigating grid imbalance in multiphase active distribution networks with distributed soft open points (SOPs). The framework comprises a wide-margin constraint barrier recourse (WCBR) module that seeks the maximal separation of constraint-compliant and unsafe actions and learns to proactively suppress exploratory violations. The framework addresses operational volatility using a novel adaptation of noncrossing quantile regression (NQR) distributional critics that track the complete distribution of policy returns. The set of behavior and recourse policies integrates an instantaneous physics-based and differentiable action projection mechanism that generates SOP constraint-compliant actions without relying on active learning. Policy safety is made responsive using an enhancement of conventional experience replay, and the safety performance of the framework is supported by probabilistic bounds derived in the paper. The proposed framework was trained and tested on a modified multiphase IEEE 123-bus test feeder. Results demonstrate its superiority to conventional reinforcement learning and SRL methods and show that it is highly competitive against the nonlinear AC optimal power flow.

papers.title: Co-simulation-Based Safety-Assessment of Black-Box Maritime Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.summary: Modern maritime cyber-physical systems consist of tightly interconnected subsystems ranging from multiple engineering domains, making exhaustive safety verification impractical. Simulation-based testing offers a scalable alternative, while co-simulation enables heterogeneous subsystem models, potentially developed by different stakeholders, to be integrated without requiring access to their internal implementations. Adaptive Stress-Testing further improves testing efficiency by formulating failure discovery as a sequential decision-making problem, guiding the search toward the most likely failure scenarios, and giving the counter safety examples using reinforcement learning. However, black-box co-simulation may provide only partial access to the system state required by conventional Markov decision process formulations. To address this limitation, we proposed Event-Based Adaptive Stress-Testing version 2, a co-simulation-based safety-assessment method formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process. This method employs Recurrent Proximal Policy Optimization to exploit observation histories when selecting adversarial actions. The method is evaluated on a ship-in-transit operation in which a collision-avoidance system is stress-tested against multi-adversarial target ships. An extended Intermediate Waypoint Sampling mechanism enables independent multi-adversary trajectory control and supports the generation of realistic collision-inducing scenarios. The experiment demonstrate that the learned stress-testing policy generalizes across different encounter cases, can be further improved through continued training, and can be made effective when the collision- avoidance system under test is replaced by another version. These results demonstrate the method's potential for scalable black-box safety assessment of complex maritime cyber-physical systems.

papers.title: Data-Driven Factored Abstractions of Stochastic Systems
papers.summary: Formal verification and correct-by-design policy synthesis for stochastic dynamical systems face significant scalability challenges due to the curse of dimensionality. These challenges are exacerbated when the system dynamics are unknown and abstractions must be constructed from data. This paper introduces a data-driven framework for constructing factored interval Markov decision process (fIMDP) abstractions from noisy transition observations. Assuming conditional independence of successor coordinates and known coordinate-wise Lipschitz bounds on the dynamics, the framework estimates marginal transition probabilities rather than joint probabilities, resulting in an exponential reduction in the number of probability entries to be estimated and stored. We establish finite-sample confidence guarantees that the abstraction captures the concrete transition probabilities uniformly over each abstract region, enabling certified lower bounds on satisfaction probabilities for $ω$-regular specifications. Experiments on benchmark systems, including pendulum swing-up, unicycle control, and a four-dimensional planar robot model, demonstrate improvements in certified satisfaction probability lower bounds of up to 25 percentage points compared with a state-of-the-art flat IMDP abstraction method. Our framework required up to 23x less memory and was consistently faster in constructing the abstraction.

papers.title: Impedance-Aware Optimized Pulse Patterns for Reconfigurable Battery Systems
papers.summary: Reconfigurable battery systems (RBS) synthesize the converter output voltage by inserting and bypassing battery cell groups, so every switching state changes not only the source voltage but also the source impedance. This paper shows that this configuration-dependent impedance breaks a tacit assumption of optimized pulse patterns (OPP): patterns designed with the customary linear plant model overestimate their achievable current quality by up to an order of magnitude and converge to a distortion floor set by the resistance modulation. We propose impedance-aware optimized pulse patterns (IA-OPP), which embed the level-dependent source impedance in the optimization objective, combined with an event-budget formulation that treats the reconfiguration rate of the communication bus as a managed resource. An exact closed-form evaluation of the piecewise-exponential load current renders the objective smooth in the switching instants. In a simulated cascaded-bridge reference system, IA-OPP attains 0.52% current total harmonic distortion (THD) at a reconfiguration rate of 2.4 kHz, outperforming nearest-level modulation, phase-shifted carrier pulse-width modulation (PWM) at up to five times the switching rate, and a classical OPP baseline at every event budget; the advantage persists across the modulation-index range and under +-30% parameter mismatch. For three-wire star-connected systems, masking triplen orders in the objective restores the full advantage, with the impedance-aware patterns beating their linear-model counterparts by about 20% at equal budget.

papers.title: Transmission Expansion and Energy Storage Planning under Great Britain's Uncertain Energy Transition Pathways
papers.summary: Long term power system planning must account for uncertainty in electricity demand and generation, while recognising the different investment and commissioning characteristics of transmission and energy storage. This paper develops a multi year stochastic framework for coordinated transmission expansion and energy storage planning and applies it to the Great Britain electricity system to assess investment needs through to 2050. The framework integrates multiple energy transition pathways with an enhanced representation of the GB transmission network and captures the different characteristics of transmission and storage investment over time. The coordinated treatment of transmission and storage is considered as a system level benchmark rather than a centralised investment mechanism. In GB, transmission investment is subject to regulated forward looking planning, while storage is largely developed by market participants in response to market signals. The framework therefore quantifies the potential value of improved coordination and identifies where existing investment signals may not encourage complementary storage deployment. Results across alternative transmission only, storage only and coordinated investment strategies show substantial benefits from joint planning. Compared with transmission only planning, coordinated investment reduces additional transmission capacity by 2%, cumulative expected load shedding by 97%, and total expected system cost by 36%, primarily through avoided unserved energy. Transmission preparation periods affect the timing, but not the final portfolio, of investments. Finally, the energy transition pathway materially influences investment requirements, with Electrification and Efficiency requiring 7% more transmission capacity and 45% more storage energy capacity than Falling Behind.

papers.title: Dynamic Flexibility Requests in Local Flexibility Markets: Quantifying the DSO Willingness to Pay
papers.summary: Local Flexibility Markets (LFMs) require Distribution System Operators (DSOs) to determine both the quantity of flexibility to procure and the corresponding willingness to pay during market clearing. Existing approaches typically rely on centralized AC-OPF clearing algorithms with limited practical scalability or strictly localized, static flexibility requests driven primarily by congestion management, while the economic value of flexibility is largely neglected. This paper proposes a dynamic flexibility-request methodology in which the DSO's willingness to pay is embedded directly into the market-clearing objective by monetizing transformer and cable aging, network losses, and voltage congestion. To enable computationally efficient clearing, exact convex piecewise-linear epigraph reformulations of the IEEE C57.91 transformer aging model and an Arrhenius-based cable aging model are developed and formally proven to preserve exactness. The proposed framework is validated on a modified CIGRE MV benchmark and compared with a recent state-of-the-art flexibility-request methodology. The results demonstrate significantly higher market liquidity, more efficient flexibility procurement, and improved network operations while preserving the market's transparency and non-discrimination principles.

papers.title: MARS: Feature-guided physics-informed deep learning for real-time battery health and lifetime prediction
papers.summary: Accurate and robust estimation of battery state-of-health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) is essential for safe and cost-effective operation of electrified transportation systems, yet it remains challenging under operating variability, non-stationary aging, and non-Gaussian measurement disturbances. This paper proposes Multi-scale Adaptive Robust State Estimation (MARS), a multi-scale adaptive robust state-estimation framework that couples a dual-branch temporal encoder with an equivalent-circuit-model-constrained differentiable generalized-correntropy adaptive Kalman filter. The encoder disentangles fast intra-cycle voltage-current-temperature dynamics from slow inter-cycle degradation, and the fused degradation context adaptively parameterizes the cycle-level process covariance, measurement covariance, and correntropy bandwidth. Through the unrolled robust filtering recursion, MARS performs physics-consistent state propagation and generalized-correntropy-based innovation correction, while uncertainty decomposition and Monte Carlo dropout provide calibrated prediction intervals for SOH estimation and conditional RUL prediction. Experiments on the NASA and CALCE benchmarks demonstrate improved SOH accuracy, achieving mean absolute error/root mean square error values of 0.72%/0.92% and 0.63%/0.80%, respectively, together with competitive conditional RUL performance against representative data-driven and hybrid baselines. The resulting conditional-RUL prediction intervals achieve coverage probabilities of 100.00% and 99.24% on NASA and CALCE, respectively. Ablation, disturbance-sensitivity, near-end-of-life, and runtime analyses further verify the contribution of each module and the practical inference cost for online battery management.

papers.title: Mean-Field Learning for Storage Aggregation
papers.summary: Distributed energy storage devices can be aggregated to provide operational flexibility for power systems. Their efficient integration into system-level optimization calls for an accurate and computationally tractable surrogate that jointly represents aggregate flexibility and operating costs. However, constructing such a surrogate is challenging due to device heterogeneity, nonconvex operating constraints, and high-dimensional power trajectories. To address these challenges, this paper develops a mean-field learning framework for storage aggregation. Using random-set expectations, we show that the joint representation of aggregate flexibility and operating costs converges almost surely to a deterministic convex mean-field limit. This limit provides a learning benchmark for storage aggregation, against which we bound the approximation error of any convex surrogate. These theoretical results motivate a convex virtual-battery surrogate with physically interpretable parameters. We learn these parameters through a bilevel optimization problem that matches the optimal values of the surrogate and the storage fleet when both respond to a set of price scenarios. We derive closed-form gradients to solve this problem efficiently. Case studies illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the framework's approximation accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to device heterogeneity.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Synthesis of Contraction Metrics with Certified Verification
papers.summary: We study counterexample-guided synthesis of contraction metrics for continuous-time autonomous systems on compact domains. A learner proposes a metric; a sound verifier certifies its matrix inequality or returns diagnostic points for retraining. The neural extension pairs a learned metric factor with symbolic contraction conditions and rigorous numerical verification; main ablations use polynomial features. We give computable polynomial bounds in arbitrary dimension and outward-rounded verification for polynomial, trigonometric, and neural representations. Loop soundness is separated from conditional finite-grid termination under idealized feasibility assumptions. We analyze why scaling and fixed-margin training can leave valid metrics uncertified. The scaling construction requires a scale-closed family, which the experimental fixed-floor class generally lacks. Verified slack improves the contraction rate and quantifies model-error tolerances using certified residual and Jacobian bounds. Finite-distance conclusions require connecting paths whose flows stay in the verified region. Experiments include controlled ablations, three-dimensional verification, and transfer from a fitted surrogate with known-truth residual certification. A physical swing-model study compares neural learning objectives with shared verification and invariant energy regions. Verified constant metrics certify the polynomial benchmark and smallest swing-model domain; neither result requires neural state dependence. Exploratory refinement certifies additional frozen candidates at a larger verification budget. In matched polynomial operating-grid experiments, trace normalization and margin coupling did not demonstrate a certification-count advantage within the tested budgets. These choices address specific failure mechanisms without guaranteeing optimizer convergence or general empirical superiority.

papers.title: Online Neural Network Training via Closed-Loop Model-Free Tracking Control: An Empirical Study
papers.summary: Training artificial neural networks predominantly relies on offline, gradient-based backpropagation algorithms. In contrast, biological circuits process and retain information through decentralized, continuous-time adaptation. papers.title: Finite-Step Algorithms for Input-Constrained Control Barrier Function-Based Safety Filters
papers.summary: Control barrier function (CBF) safety filters commonly rely on quadratic programs (QPs) to modify nominal control inputs while satisfying safety constraints. For safety-critical applications, however, the solution must be computed reliably under actuator limitations and with predictable computational effort. General-purpose QP solvers typically rely on numerical convergence criteria, which do not directly provide finite bounds on algorithmic steps or distinguish solver failure from mathematical infeasibility. This paper considers CBF-QPs with a single affine safety constraint, componentwise input bounds, and diagonal quadratic weights. Exploiting the established scalar dual structure of continuous quadratic knapsack problems, we obtain a necessary and sufficient pointwise feasibility condition and an exact breakpoint-based solution procedure. The algorithm requires at most 2n positive breakpoint events for n inputs, reducing to at most n events when the nominal input is admissible. In the latter case, an exact saturation--redistribution algorithm computes the optimal solution in at most n passes. We further describe how the structured solution can be combined with verified floating-point constraint evaluation to distinguish certified feasible commands, certified infeasibility, and unresolved numerical cases. The resulting framework provides an exact and computationally predictable solution procedure for a practically relevant class of input-constrained CBF safety filters.

papers.title: G-RADI: A Low-Rank ADI Algorithm for General-Form Large-Scale Continuous-Time Algebraic Riccati Equations
papers.summary: Continuous-time algebraic Riccati equations (CAREs) arise in numerous disciplines and can be written in several forms. When the coefficient matrices are small and dense, stabilizing solutions can be computed for all these forms. The situation differs for large-scale sparse problems: for CAREs in general form, only a reformulation of the Newton--Kleinman iteration is currently available. The low-rank alternating direction implicit (ADI) algorithm for CAREs, known as Riccati-ADI (RADI), is among the most successful and computationally efficient methods in the literature. However, RADI applies only to simplified forms of CAREs; no low-rank ADI algorithm is available for CAREs in general form. This paper presents a low-rank ADI algorithm for CAREs in general form, which contains RADI as a special case. Unlike the Newton--Kleinman iteration, which computes a new approximation at every step, the proposed algorithm---like RADI---recursively accumulates low-rank factors of an approximation to the stabilizing solution. Moreover, the residual admits a low-rank factorization, so its norm can be computed efficiently; in the Newton--Kleinman iteration, computing the residual norm is considerably more involved. An automatic shift-generation strategy is also proposed, enabling the algorithm to select its shifts without user input. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems with orders ranging from \(10^6\) to \(10^7\) show that the proposed method is accurate and computationally efficient, and that it outperforms the Newton--Kleinman iteration.

papers.title: Model-Free Stealthy Attack on Vehicle Systems and Its Implications for ISO/SAE 21434 Risk Assessment
papers.summary: This paper investigates a model-free stealthy adversary targeting in-vehicle networks and its implications for automotive cybersecurity risk assessment. In a closed-loop lane-keeping benchmark, the attack induces a 1.25 m lateral displacement, exceeding the specified 0.9 m half-lane width, and keeps the vehicle outside the lane corridor for 9.21 s. papers.title: Quantale-Enriched Co-Design: Toward a Framework for Quantitative Heterogeneous System Design
papers.summary: Monotone co-design enables compositional engineering design by modeling components as feasibility relations between required resources and provided functionalities. papers.title: Classical heat exchanger fouling-resistance laws as first-moment identities of additive stochastic deposition

papers.title: Transient State Preservation of a Dissipative Qubit via Lyapunov Control
papers.summary: Preserving quantum states in the presence of environmental decoherence remains a fundamental challenge for quantum information processing. This work investigates whether Hamiltonian Lyapunov feedback can transiently preserve the state of an open qubit by reshaping its trajectory under Markovian dissipation. A state-error Lyapunov function is adopted to derive an analytical feedback law for Lindblad dynamics, ensuring a nonincreasing Lyapunov function whenever the control sensitivities are nonzero. The analysis identifies the geometric conditions under which the feedback becomes ineffective, showing that control authority vanishes when the current and target Bloch vectors are collinear. Numerical simulations are performed for amplitude damping and pure dephasing using selected target states. Performance is evaluated through fidelity, accumulated infidelity, dwell time above a fidelity threshold, coherence, and control effort. The results demonstrate that the proposed feedback cannot eliminate irreversible dissipation or achieve universal asymptotic stabilization, but it can provide transient benefits for selected target-channel combinations. In particular, under amplitude damping, the controller significantly reduces accumulated infidelity and substantially extends the interval during which the system remains above a prescribed fidelity threshold. In the pure dephasing cases examined, improvements in fidelity are generally limited, although transient coherence preservation is observed for the oblique target considered, revealing a trade-off between coherence and state fidelity. These findings indicate that Lyapunov-based Hamiltonian feedback is best suited as a transient preservation mechanism and motivate its application to gate operations and preservation of prepared states during finite time intervals before their use or readout.

papers.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback
papers.summary: We study a time-slotted generate-at-will status-update system over an erasure channel with transmission success probability $q$, subject to average sampling- and transmission-rate constraints $f_s$ and $f_r$, respectively. The sampler-transmitter pair jointly decides whether to idle, retransmit a stale packet, or replace it with a fresh sample. We derive a universal lower bound on the optimal average age of information, analyze a class of stationary randomized policies, and obtain an optimal policy within this class that provides a $4$-approximation guarantee. The joint problem reduces to the sampling-constrained problem when $f_s\leq qf_r$ and the transmission-constrained problem when $f_s\geq f_r$. For $qf_r<f_s<f_r$, we formulate a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) and introduce the class $\barΠ$ of $(W,R)$ policies, where $W$ specifies a waiting threshold for transmission and $R$ specifies a packet-replacement threshold. We prove that, for every choice of Lagrange multipliers, the corresponding Lagrangian-relaxed Markov decision process admits an optimal policy in $\barΠ$. We then formulate a linear program (LP) over distributions of $(W,R)$ policies and prove that choosing a policy according to an optimal LP solution yields an optimal CMDP policy. Moreover, there exists an optimal LP solution assigning positive probability to at most three $(W,R)$ policies. Since $\barΠ$ is countably infinite, for every $ε>0$ we construct a finite subset $\barΠ_ε\subset\barΠ$ and show that the LP restricted to this set yields an $ε$-optimal policy. Finally, we derive a stronger pair of lower bounds by considering systems with only the sampling-rate or transmission-rate constraint. Using these bounds, we construct a policy randomizing among four $(W,R)$ policies with a $2$-approximation guarantee for $qf_r<f_s<f_r$.

papers.title: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.

papers.title: Input-to-State Stability in Distributed Adaptive Identification of Nonlinear Systems without Input Sharing
papers.summary: This paper studies continuous-time distributed adaptive identification of unknown nonlinear systems over directed communication networks without requiring source or neighboring inputs to be shared. Each sensing node reconstructs the source state while adapting local estimates of the unknown linear and nonlinear dynamics using only locally available information and neighboring state estimates. A network-level error representation is derived to characterize the interaction among the communication topology, observer dynamics, parameter uncertainty, and nonlinear mismatch. Norm-based, structured Lyapunov, and robust LMI conditions are established to guarantee that the resulting coupling operator is Hurwitz. Unlike the corresponding discrete-time formulation, the proposed continuous-time adaptive laws do not require normalization. A Lyapunov analysis establishes boundedness of the adaptive parameters and asymptotic convergence of the estimation and source-tracking errors in the unperturbed case. Input-to-state stability is further established under bounded predictor mismatch and source disturbances. Numerical studies over star, cyclic, and path topologies support the theoretical results and demonstrate approximately linear computational scaling with the number of sensing nodes.

papers.title: Robust Action Clusters and Cascades in Opinion Dynamics with Heterogeneous Action Thresholds
papers.summary: We study the preservation and propagation of public actions in networks whose agents hold continuous private opinions. Agents update their opinions from their neighbors' observed actions and express them through action rules whose thresholds differ across agents. We characterize groups of agents that preserve a given common action regardless of the outsiders' actions. We call such a group, paired with that action, a robust action cluster. We show that a group is a robust action cluster for that action if and only if each member places enough of its influence weight on the group, where the required influence depends on the member's own action rule. We further give a sufficient condition under which an agent outside the cluster permanently adopts the cluster's action, and we iterate it to obtain a cascade of agents that are guaranteed to adopt that action. Finally, numerical examples show that replacing heterogeneous thresholds by their mean can change both the propagation of an action and the presence of robust action clusters.

papers.title: Harmonic-Constrained Hosting Capacity of Active Distribution Networks Using ESS Compensation and Certified Adaptive Decision-Tree Envelopes
papers.summary: Active distribution networks increasingly rely on coordinated inverter-based resources to accommodate renewable generation, while harmonic limits constrain the capacity that can be connected. A disaggregated mixed-integer formulation embeds these envelopes in a second-order-cone-relaxed network model. Annual hourly data are assessed through daily capacity optimization, followed by componentwise capacity aggregation and chronological full-year feasibility validation. With each generator capacity bounded by its OPF reference, the proposed method recovers the complete reference allocation. Coordinated energy dispatch and harmonic compensation thus recover generation capacity within the installed ESS converter ratings.

papers.title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
papers.summary: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system state. In contrast, the integrity attacker in this study replaces the sensor measurements with fabricated data to drive the system to undesired operating conditions. Although these two threats are typically studied separately, a wireless NCS should be protected against both simultaneously, and a defence against one affects the other. We employ an observation-encoding scheme that renders the eavesdropper's state-estimation error covariance unbounded under packet drops, and show that transmission energy governs how long this error remains bounded. In particular, lower transmission energy improves confidentiality. For integrity protection, we combine stochastic physical watermarking with a CUSUM-based sequential change detector. The proposed attack detection scheme accounts for intermittent communication and encoded measurements. The detection delay is governed by the Kullback--Leibler divergence (KLD) between the pre- and post-attack distributions of the test signal, and we show that a higher transmission energy increases the KLD and thereby reduces the detection delay. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the eavesdropper's estimation error and the worst-case expected KLD, providing guidelines for selecting transmission energy to balance confidentiality and integrity protection and characterising the privacy--security trade-off. Finally, we run numerical simulations to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the privacy--security trade-off in practical scenarios.

papers.title: Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
papers.summary: Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. papers.title: Robust Optimal Network Reduction for Distribution Systems
papers.summary: Network reduction replaces large networks with smaller equivalents to speed up power flow and optimization studies. Optimal Kron-based Reduction of Networks (Opti-KRON) finds the optimal set of nodes to faithfully represent a large-scale radial network for representative loading scenarios. papers.title: Slower but Faster: When Self-Organized Traffic Flows Beat Traffic Signal Control
papers.summary: Urban traffic flow networks are complex adaptive systems, whose variability challenges centralized, top-down control. We study decentralized alternatives in which order emerges from local interactions, comparing the network-wide performance of roundabouts in SUMO against fixed-time and actuated control as well as self-organizing signals on a 4$\times$4 grid and a rewired, irregular variant of it, across demand levels and periodic surge amplitudes. In our computer simulations of the regular grid, converting the single most central intersection already lowers delays by 2 to 3\% relative to actuated control; each additional conversion lowers them further, and full conversion outperforms every signalized alternative under all conditions studied. In the irregular traffic flow network with full conversion of all intersections into roundabouts, this holds only up to a critical load, where traffic flow breaks down sharply, when the time-averaged demand reaches about 3.1 times the base load. Beyond that point, the self-organizing traffic signals show the lowest delay of any network-wide strategy and is nearly insensitive to surges. Interestingly, roundabouts are favorable solutions even at lower speed limits: in the regular grid, compared to the mean speed under actuated control at a speed limit of 50\,km/h, roundabouts match that speed at a speed limit of about 40\,km/h. Compared to traffic signal control, this establishes a slower-is-faster effect. Furthermore, travel times in self-organized traffic flows are more predictable than in networks with conventional signals.

papers.title: Digital Twin Enabled Talkative Power Conversion
papers.summary: Talkative Power Conversion (TPC) is a paradigm in which communication is integrated directly into switched-mode power electronic converters (PECs) by modulating their inherent switching ripple. TPC enables simultaneous power transfer and information exchange without dedicated transmitter-side communication hardware, and avoids additional wiring. This paper combines, for the first time, the Digital Twin (DT) concept with the TPC paradigm. By establishing interaction between one or several physical power converters and their virtual counterpart(s), the DT framework enables enhanced modeling, prediction, and optimization of individual or networked PECs. We distinguish three coupling architectures--embedded DT, remote DT, and networked DT--and demonstrate the added value of combining DT and TPC concepts when the DT and PEC are not co-located. The proposed framework is based on state-space modeling in conjunction with Kalman filtering and facilitates joint treatment of data transmission, parameter estimation, and system operation, thereby improving robustness, adaptability, and power efficiency. The presented approach highlights the potential of DT-enhanced TPC as a key enabler for future cyber-physical energy systems with tightly integrated power and communication functionalities.

papers.title: Hands-On Beyond Classrooms: Elevating Control Engineering Education with Take-Home Labs
papers.summary: This study shows how take-home laboratories can be integrated into control engineering education to strengthen hands-on learning in both introductory and advanced courses. The work provides evidence that a compact experimental platform can support conceptual understanding, student engagement, and course performance in a broadly applicable way. Control engineering courses often rely heavily on theory and simulation, which may limit students' ability to connect abstract concepts with practical implementation. Low-cost take-home laboratories offer a scalable alternative that can help bridge this gap across different educational settings. The curricular change, consisting of the introduction of take-home laboratory kits into the semester projects, was intended to improve students' motivation, deepen their understanding of core control principles, and enhance their performance in coursework and final assessment. Students used the kits for modeling, identification, and control design tasks, while learning outcomes were evaluated through questionnaires, midterm test scores, and final exam grades. Student feedback indicated strong acceptance of the new format and improved understanding of the subject matter. Statistical analysis showed a significant difference between cohorts before and after the curricular change, with modest but measurable effect sizes. The results suggest that take-home laboratories can support both motivation and academic performance, while also improving students' appreciation of the practical relevance of control engineering.

papers.title: Learning to Clear Peer-to-Peer Energy Markets
papers.summary: Peer-to-peer energy markets are a promising paradigm for integrating distributed energy resources. A large body of work models their clearing as distributed optimization or generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems which let prosumers coordinate trades and local resources without a central operator. papers.title: A Hybrid Systems Approach to Parameterizing the PERC1 Model for Data Centers Using Synchrophasor Measurements
papers.summary: The Power Electronic Reconnecting and Ceasing (PERC1) load model represents the timed ceasing and reconnection of large power-electronic loads, including data centers. Voltage thresholds and timers govern its response, with a ramp on reconnection, making it a hybrid dynamical system. This paper formulates PERC1 as a hybrid automaton and uses that structure to identify its parameters from synchrophasor records of grid disturbances. We propose a four-stage identification procedure: mode-sequence identification, estimation of logic parameters from event-time constraints, and joint Gauss-Newton refinement using hybrid trajectory sensitivities and saltation matrices. The resulting salted Fisher information is then used to analyze parameter identifiability. Two structural results are established. The detection and actuation delays are identifiable only through their sum unless a second dip interrupts the reconnection ramp, and a single disturbance leaves one unidentifiable direction in each threshold-delay pair, which two disturbances with different voltage slopes resolve. A case study using synthetic 60 frames/s synchrophasor records demonstrates recovery of the ceasing and reconnection dynamics and identifies poorly observable parameters.

papers.title: LZn : Robust LoRa Frame Synchronization Under Frame Collisions and Ultra-Low SNR Conditions
papers.summary: LoRa has become a widely adopted wireless modulation scheme in LPWANs due to its low cost, long range, and minimal transmission power. However, collisions between frames of the same spreading factor -- common in dense LoRa deployments -- prevent conventional LoRa receivers from detecting and correctly decoding frames. Recent work has introduced methods to improve recovery, yet their detection stage degrades sharply under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and high collision rates. In this work, we introduce LZn, a synchronization scheme driven by a minimum-based spectral intersection across consecutive symbols. While preamble search incurs a modest overhead, LZn reduces the cost of fine synchronization by two to three orders of magnitude compared to existing collision-tolerant receivers. Our method enables robust frame synchronization even under multiple packet overlaps or extremely low SNR conditions. We evaluate LZn on simulations and three independent, real-world LoRa datasets. LZn improves detection sensitivity by up to 10 dB and increases detection probability by up to 1.54x. In real-world datasets, LZn improves decoding by 3.46x in the most challenging single-user scenario and up to 1.22x in collision scenarios compared to the second best collision-tolerant scheme (TnB). These results demonstrate that LZn substantially improves the frame recovery of LoRa receivers, while remaining compatible with real-time requirements.

papers.title: Intransigence or compromise: concatenated opinion dynamics with voting feedback
papers.summary: In this paper, we study opinion evolution in a sequence of Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) models, concatenated so that the final opinions of each model serve as the initial opinions of the next. Each FJ model is followed by a vote, and each agent becomes partially or fully stubborn in the next model, depending on how close its opinion is to the voting result. With the state-dependent switching of stubbornness, the dynamics are not guaranteed to be contractive. We show that, over any fixed strongly connected network, the opinions always converge. A sufficient condition on the initial opinions is proposed, under which consensus is reached exponentially fast. For the complete graph, we further show that, if the agents' stubbornness levels do not differ too much, an agent that is partially stubborn in one FJ model can never become fully stubborn in a subsequent one: once it has started compromising, it keeps doing so.

papers.title: Switched Control of Complex-Valued Kuramoto Networks
papers.summary: Synchronization in networks of coupled oscillators is classically studied via the Kuramoto model, whose intrinsic nonlinearity limits analytical tractability and complicates control design. Additionally, we present a non-autonomous complex-valued MIMO sliding-mode controller that enforces phase locking at a prescribed frequency in finite time, regardless of natural frequencies and coupling strengths, under appropriate control gain selection. papers.title: Verification-Guided Safety-Repair of Learned Controllers
papers.summary: Formal verification can certify that a learned controller is safe. But what should be done when verification fails? Simply suppressing actions that lead to unsafe next states is insufficient because the dangerous action that ultimately caused the safety violation might have occurred many steps earlier. Retraining modifies the policy globally, thereby potentially introducing new failures. Instead, we introduce ReachECO, a verification-guided repair procedure that exploits the information of failed multi-step reachability analysis for synthesizing explicit constraints on controller behavior. For Differentiable Weightless Controllers, the repairs compile into exact circuit patches that leave the controller unchanged everywhere outside the targeted policy cells. We prove soundness and termination of the repair procedure for ReachECO, as well as, assuming exhaustive continuation search, completeness relative to the reachability abstraction. papers.title: A Lifted Hessian-Riemannian Gradient Flow for LQR Synthesis under Passivity Constraints
papers.summary: The static state-feedback gain that renders a linear system passive at an external port and minimizes a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost cannot be computed by convex optimization, since the passivity certificate and the LQR cost are coupled bilinearly through the common gain. Numerical examples show that the flow attains a lower cost than the indirect approach, that the completion is required for multi-input systems, and that the flow can converge to a local minimizer on nonconvex passivity regions.

papers.title: Contingency Planning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Vehicles: A Review and Perspectives
papers.summary: Contingency planning is an architectural capability that enables autonomous vehicles (AVs) to anticipate and mitigate safety risks arising from safety-relevant logical-mode transitions, such as sensor outages and uncertain interactions. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the field, synthesizing fragmented literature into a unified logic-conditioned hybrid control framework. Within this formalism, we categorize approaches into two distinct paradigms: Reactive Safety enforces safety constraints or activates fallback actions after a contingency mode has been observed or reliably inferred, whereas Proactive Safety preserves recourse across unresolved mode alternatives through non-anticipative branching. In addition, we propose a fine-grained taxonomy that partitions the landscape into external contingencies (environmental and interactive hazards) and internal contingencies (system faults). Our analysis reveals a fundamental structural divergence: internal faults are predominantly addressed via reactive fail-safe mechanisms, whereas external interaction uncertainties increasingly require proactive branching strategies. Furthermore, we identify a critical methodological divergence: whereas physical hazards are typically managed with formal guarantees, semantic and out-of-distribution anomalies currently rely heavily on empirical validation. We conclude by identifying the open challenges in bridging the gap between theoretical guarantees and practical validation, advocating for hybrid architectures and standardized benchmarking to transition contingency planning from formulation to certifiable real-world deployment.

papers.title: Toward Operationalizing Rasmussen in Evolving Software Systems
papers.summary: Rasmussen's qualitative drift model explains how successive, locally successful adaptations under efficiency pressures can move a system toward unacceptable operation. It tracks how activity or resource use is distributed across components and types of work. Measurement history quantifies accumulated change and recent movement toward or away from current limits. papers.title: Sub-Synchronous Control Interaction Risk of Large Data Center Loads: A Frequency-Scan Assessment with Cross-Model Validation

papers.title: Stability Despite Misalignment: Model Predictive Game Controllers with Objective Misspecifications
papers.summary: Predictive control requires the controller to possess an embedded prediction model. We provide sufficient conditions for the stability of multi-agent dynamical systems with heterogeneous MPG controllers adopting linear-quadratic (LQ) games. We also show that misaligned game models can destabilize a system that reaches stability when all agents share the same game model, using a financial duopoly simulation.

papers.title: Adjacent Heat Transfer Effects Can Bias Savings Estimates When Controlling Only Part of a Multi-Zone Building
papers.summary: Field demonstrations of advanced heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning control often operate a few thermal zones within a larger building and report savings for those zones alone. papers.title: STA: A Split Temporal Adversary Method for Evaluating Robustness of Multimodal RL-based Driving Policies
papers.summary: Multimodal reinforcement learning (MRL) offers a promising paradigm for autonomous driving by jointly leveraging complementary sensor observations to learn effective decision-making policies. STA includes two mechanisms: a) a unified multimodal temporal perturbation mechanism that delays observations via historical states, removing the need for modality-specific noise; b) a split multimodal adversarial decision mechanism that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection through adaptive optimization while leveraging the victim policy's clean actions to identify sensitive decision patterns. Experiments in the CARLA simulator show that STA more than doubles the collision rate of the strongest baseline against PPO while using 17.8\% fewer attack attempts, and that it generalizes to a VLM-based driving policy. papers.title: BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Camera-based driving models build a dense bird's-eye-view (BEV) grid and spend the same computation on every cell of it, although the vehicle crosses only a few of those cells within the planning horizon. papers.title: SAFER: Navigating the Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma in World-Model-Based Planning for Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. A world model offers this foresight, but only within the coverage of its training data, which poses an exploration-exploitation dilemma. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes, 0.95 and 0.77 from a privileged bird's-eye view, and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive, 53.4 in regular and 49.0 in safety-critical traffic. papers.title: Teaching VLMs What to Say, Not How to Reason: Rethinking Counterfactual Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: End-to-end autonomous driving systems have been shown to suffer from shortcut learning and causal confusion, limiting their ability to generalize robustly under distribution shift. To mitigate these limitations, recent works based on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have explored incorporating linguistic reasoning capabilities into driving decision-making, reporting improvements in driving performance. In particular, counterfactual (CF) reasoning has been proposed to enable self-reflective, high-level causal understanding. However, it remains unclear whether the language-based reasoning mitigates shortcut learning or merely shifts it from visual representations to linguistic patterns, creating an illusion of causal understanding. Moreover, existing approaches often conflate intervention-based reasoning with CF reasoning, leaving the effects of genuine CF reasoning unexplored. In this work, we examine what CF reasoning actually induces in VLM-based autonomous driving and observe that it shifts the action distribution toward more conservative behaviors while increasing uncertainty in reasoning and decision-making. This effect persists under reinforcement fine-tuning, suggesting that it is not merely a transient artifact. Furthermore, visual attention analysis shows that CF reasoning does not alter visual grounding, while causal intervention experiments reveal that masking causally relevant and non-causal factors in accident scenarios results in comparable decision change rates. Overall, these results suggest that CF reasoning does not induce genuine causal reasoning grounded in visual evidence. Instead, it acts as a linguistic shortcut that reshapes the action distribution, teaching models what to say but not how to reason, highlighting a gap between language-based reasoning and causal understanding in autonomous driving.

papers.title: TrajWAM: Trajectory-Conditioned Future Learning for Vision-Language Driving
papers.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) connect future scene prediction with action planning for autonomous driving. Each driving record pairs an executed ego trajectory with its observed future, providing a factual outcome for learning this connection. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-conditioned WAM that improves vision-language driving through auxiliary bird's-eye-view (BEV) future learning. An ego-trajectory query conditions DINOv3-aligned BEV predictions from shared planner representations. Training combines factual reconstruction under the executed trajectory with one-sided feature separation under an unlabeled perturbed trajectory. Together, these objectives train the shared planner to generate driving waypoints. Native inference directly generates waypoints and bypasses the auxiliary future-prediction branch. On all 220 Bench2Drive routes, TrajWAM achieves 91.53 Driving Score and 75.45% Success Rate, exceeding a schedule-matched planning-only fine-tuning baseline by 5.31 Driving Score points and eight successful routes.

papers.title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
papers.summary: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

papers.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual analysis. We perform our analysis on more than 80,000 synthetic driving scenes using an autonomous vehicle based on PlanT 2.0, a state-of-the-art Transformer-based model for object-level planning. Results show that attention provides a correlational rather than causal indication of object relevance. Attention-based relevance estimation methods do not consistently identify all relevant objects and tend to incorrectly classify as relevant objects with little or no impact on the vehicle's driving. In particular, results show that attention can effectively identify relevant objects in simple single-lane, straight-road scenarios, but its accuracy degrades in more complex settings, such as multi-lane roads and intersections. These findings highlight the limitations of attention as a proxy for object relevance, calling for novel methods able to accurately capture the causal impact of individual objects on the vehicle's driving and distinguish it from correlational associations.

papers.title: VoxSAOR: Semantic-Aware Occupancy Robustification via Aleatoric Uncertainty Modeling
papers.summary: Vision-based 3D occupancy prediction provides a dense semantic representation of scenes for autonomous driving and embodied perception, yet remains vulnerable to occlusion, depth ambiguity, and projection errors that induce spatially varying reliability in voxel features. Existing methods typically map voxel representations to semantic predictions without explicitly modeling such observation-induced feature variations. To address this limitation, we propose VoxSAOR, a semantic-aware occupancy robustification framework that models aleatoric uncertainty through feature-space proxies. It first quantifies Local Semantic Consistency (LSC) to derive a voxel-wise structural stability prior and uses cross-view semantic consensus to filter unreliable semantic correspondences. Within each semantic category, spatially matched stable and ambiguous voxels form stable-to-ambiguous feature transitions, which are modeled by a class-conditional diagonal Gaussian distribution, capturing both feature displacement and dispersion. Guided by these proxy distributions, Aleatoric Regime Ensemble Learning (AREL) trains independently parameterized prediction heads using feature perturbations at progressively increasing scales, with perturbation strength modulated by structural reliability. At inference, proxy modeling and sampling are disabled, and all heads process the same observed features; their output probabilities are then averaged to produce a deterministic consensus prediction without requiring sampling. Experiments across multiple datasets and occupancy backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of VoxSAOR in improving semantic occupancy prediction, long-tail recognition, and predictive calibration. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/VoxSAOR.

papers.title: AcousticBEV: Acoustic BEV Object Localization for Intelligent Vehicles
papers.summary: Modern autonomous driving and driver assistance systems rely predominantly on cameras, radars and LiDARs for environmental perception. However, these modalities face different environmental limitations, including poor illumination for cameras and adverse weather for LiDAR. Acoustic sensing, particularly using microphone arrays, could provide complementary perception capabilities for autonomous driving, but has remained largely underexplored. In this work, we design a horizontally arranged microphone array that functions as the "ears" of a vehicle, enabling localization of nearby moving vehicles in a bird's-eye view (BEV) representation that captures both their relative direction and distance. Using this array, we collect a real-world driving dataset, AcousticScenes, which contains 2,117 static and 2,863 dynamic samples with synchronized spatial acoustic signals, LiDAR point clouds and 3D bounding box annotations. Building on this dataset, we propose AcousticBEV, a learning-based method for acoustic BEV object localization, which estimates the center locations of moving traffic participants in BEV from the microphone-array signals, conditioned on the ego vehicle's own speed. Experimental results demonstrate that AcousticBEV outperforms both classical signal-processing baselines and other learning-based methods, achieving F1 scores of $47.7 \pm 1.2$% on "Easy" scenarios and $45.1 \pm 1.4$% on "Difficult" cases. Our findings demonstrate that acoustic signals from a low-cost, vehicle-mounted microphone array can localize nearby moving vehicles in both azimuth and distance.

papers.title: EViDS: An Environment--Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Simulation Platform for Intelligent Chassis Development
papers.summary: The development of intelligent chassis increasingly requires the integration of environmental and perception information with high-fidelity vehicle dynamics to support environment-aware intelligent chassis control. papers.title: Passable for Whom? Few-Shot Learning for Personal Calibration of Sidewalk Accessibility Perception for Human-Centered Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Whether a sidewalk is passable depends on who is trying to pass: people who use the same mobility aid disagree about the same image, so one label per scene, or per aid, is wrong for many of them. We introduce few-shot personal accessibility perception: from K answers of a person never seen before, predict their judgment of sidewalk scenes never seen before. PassCal separates a shared description of the scene from the person's interpretation of it. The description comes from the internal state of a frozen vision-language model (VLM) and from barrier type, severity and context properties predicted by a detector trained on 14.9k public audits; the interpretation, a calibration of the person's response style and a weighting of the properties, is fit from their answers. On 8,883 judgments in which each of 135 verified mobility-aid users rated the same 50 sidewalk scenes, with people and scenes both held out, eight answers lower the Brier score from 0.550 to 0.479. The same VLM prompted with those answers reaches 0.562, and the same calibration without the scene 0.521. Conformal risk control turns predictions into passable, blocked or "depends on you" statements with a bounded expected rate of wrong statements over people; at 5%, eight answers raise the share of decisive scenes from 27% to 42%. Audit-supervised properties improve all sixteen vision and VLM encoders we test and outperform attributes from a sidewalk navigation VLM.

papers.title: VESPA: Verifiable Symbolic Policy Adaptation for Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Safe reinforcement learning (RL) aims to prevent agents from taking actions that are dangerous or destructive to their environment. This is especially important for safety-critical domains, such as robotics or autonomous driving. Formal verification can be used to prove agent safety through safety constraints. However, in practice, many policies do violate safety constraints, and thus are verified to be unsafe. Since the goal is to obtain a safe policy, we would need to retrain a new policy from scratch and then verify it again until a candidate happens to pass. Both training and verification are usually not cheap, which makes this process inefficient. We introduce VESPA ($\textbf{VE}$rifiable $\textbf{S}$ymbolic $\textbf{P}$olicy $\textbf{A}$daptation), a framework for targeted fine-tuning of decision tree policies. We show that using counterexamples for policy adaptation can make existing unsafe policies safe, or at least make considerable progress towards safety. Targeted fine-tuning of the existing policy on those counterexamples enables it to learn how to avoid violating safety constraints. We thus use the result of a formal verification as a training signal for fine-tuning. On CartPole, VESPA raises the mean number of verified safe steps from 63.8 to at least 92.7, reaching after two iterations what the same loop without counterexamples reaches after ten. On MountainCarContinuous, VESPA turns an unsafe policy into a safe policy in 53 of 60 runs. We conclude that counterexamples from a verifier are an effective training signal, which can be utilized to systematically improve the safety of policies. Our implementation is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/VESPA-Submission/

papers.title: PGU-Decoder: Prior-Guided Unified Decoding for Industrial Road-Network Map Updating
papers.summary: Timely road-network map updates are essential to navigation and autonomous driving. Three key tasks are intra-intersection road network generation, merging/diverging detection, and drivable-area detection, covering topology, geometry, and attributes, respectively. Separate pipelines duplicate rule maintenance, quality assurance, and manual verification, increasing operational costs. We propose PGU-Decoder, a production-grade unified decoding framework for semantic prediction across these tasks. A Prior Query Module (PQM) constructs point-level prior queries from sampled locations on road-network geometries. Fixed reference points preserve positional priors throughout decoding, allowing the model to focus on surrounding context. Point-level representations are aggregated into instance-level representations, and a Relational Graph Attention Network (RGAT) captures inter-instance dependencies. Task-specific heads then generate predictions. We validate PGU-Decoder in large-scale automated road-network map updating across more than 360 cities in China, where it consistently outperforms seven baselines. Following deployment at AutoNavi Map, it achieves quality scores above 98% on all three tasks, reduces manual verification costs by 95%, and increases update frequency from weekly to hourly. These results demonstrate a practical and cost-effective industrial solution for road-network map updating.

papers.title: LeViT-UNet++: Towards Balanced Fine-Grained Details and Context for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
papers.summary: Efficient medical image segmentation is essential for clinical applications requiring fast and accurate delineation, such as surgical navigation, radiation therapy, and real-time image-guided intervention. Despite substantial advances in convolutional neural networks and Transformers, attaining high accuracy under limited computational resources remains difficult, because reducing model complexity often sacrifices fine-grained structural details and global context modeling, yielding an unfavorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. To address this, we propose LeViT-UNet++, an efficient encoder-decoder architecture that better balances local detail preservation and global context modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Haar Wavelet Multi-Scale Downsampling (HWMD) module that decomposes feature representations into low- and high-frequency components to extract multi-scale structural information, thereby mitigating detail loss during downsampling. We further develop a depthwise convolution-based decoder that integrates multi-scale global representations from Transformer blocks with local spatial features, enabling progressive feature refinement while reducing computational overhead. Evaluated on four benchmarks (Synapse, ACDC, LA2018, and MSD Heart) under both 2D and 3D settings, LeViT-UNet++ achieves competitive accuracy with a compact parameter footprint and fast inference. On Synapse, for instance, it attains a DSC of 76.57% with only 8.025M parameters and 241.72 FPS, confirming a favorable accuracy-efficiency balance. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining wavelet-based multi-scale feature extraction with lightweight local-global feature fusion for efficient medical segmentation. The source code is available at https://github.com/apple1986/levit_unet_pp.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
papers.summary: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. We present GRACE, a retrieval-augmented refiner that edits an input mask under context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. The refiner is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, branching vessels, and tumour lesions. In the held-out dataset-transfer evaluation, three held-out datasets query a fixed knowledge base built from training data only. A separate leave-one-anatomy-out experiment tests parameter-free index extension: verified cases of an unseen solid organ enter the knowledge base, and the refiner stays frozen. A light shape-aware projection head on a frozen multimodal encoder maps embedding similarity to the shape agreement of the masks, so the knowledge base returns cases that the refiner can use as a shape prior. We evaluate GRACE on 18 public datasets spanning CT, MRI and ultrasound, using nine refinement configurations and seven upstream segmentors that span weak, mid, and strong operating regimes. We report each change with the DSC of its input mask. On the weak tier, the input DSC is 0.386 and GRACE adds up to +0.35 DSC. On a strong segmentor, the input DSC is 0.932 and the mean change is small. Transfer to an imaging modality that is absent from training and from the index is partial and depends on the anatomy, and remains an open research direction. Our results suggest retrieval-conditioned refinement is a practical alternative to anatomy-specific correction models. Code: https://github.com/robustml-eurecom/grace

papers.title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.summary: Object Tracking systems estimate the motion of surrounding vehicles by linking detected objects across video frames. In particular, Tracking-By-Detection (TBD) systems combine object detectors with motion prediction and data association to maintain object identities over time. Therefore, this paper evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic attacks on YOLOv3 and YOLOv4 detectors paired with SORT, Deep SORT, Strong SORT, and OC-SORT tracking systems. Under image-specific attacks, HOTA for YOLOv3-based trackers declines from 53.45-56.19% to 14.85-17.03%, while MOTA reaches -772.60% in the worst case. YOLOv4-based trackers exhibit greater robustness, while HOTA still declines to 25.06-26.86%. In addition, image-agnostic attacks can reduce the tracking accuracy using a single Universal Adversarial Perturbation (UAP), without generating a separate perturbation for individual frames.

papers.title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
papers.summary: Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolvation to molecular conformer search to adsorption on metal surfaces, with associated evaluation metrics and baselines. The result is a single set of end-to-end-trained weights that simultaneously performs all tasks and surpasses state-of-the-art models specialized for crystal structure prediction and property-conditional molecule generation. Our results demonstrate the viability of scaling generalist decoder-only models for native multimodal understanding and generation across language and chemistry. Code is available at https://github.com/the-matter-lab/nahual.

papers.title: Generating Adversarial Events: A Motion-Aware Point Cloud Framework
papers.summary: Event cameras have been widely adopted in safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving, robotics, and human-computer interaction. A pressing challenge arises from the vulnerability of deep neural networks to adversarial examples, which poses a significant threat to the reliability of event-based systems. papers.title: Algorithmic Insurance
papers.summary: When artificial intelligence (AI) systems make errors in high-stakes domains such as medical diagnosis or autonomous driving, a single algorithmic flaw across varying contexts can generate heterogeneous losses that challenge traditional insurance assumptions. Algorithmic insurance, financial coverage for AI-induced damages, is an emerging market, yet insurers struggle to price these risks and AI developers lack frameworks linking system design to liability exposure. We connect a key operational choice in binary classification, how practitioners set decision thresholds, to tail risk exposure. Using conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) to capture extreme losses, we prove that established approaches such as accuracy maximization can significantly increase worst-case losses relative to tail risk optimization, with penalties growing at least quadratically as thresholds deviate from optimal. We propose a liability insurance contract that mandates risk-aware thresholds and characterize when it creates value for AI providers, extending the analysis to degrading model performance and human oversight. In a mammography case study, accuracy-maximizing thresholds carry up to four times the tail risk of CVaR-optimal thresholds. Insurance contracts create 7-8% gains for well-calibrated firms through risk transfer and regulatory capital relief, and up to 105% for poorly calibrated firms through mandatory recalibration, while partially aligned firms can lose under a strict mandate, calling for threshold flexibility in contract design. Unlike traditional insurance that merely transfers risk, algorithmic insurance can act as both a financial instrument and an operational governance mechanism, enabling risk transfer while improving AI safety.

papers.title: Intra-Agent Motion and Inter-Agent Relation Learning for Map-Free Trajectory Prediction
papers.summary: Trajectory prediction is essential for safe planning and decision-making in autonomous driving. Map-free prediction improves deployment flexibility by removing the dependence on high-definition maps, but it also loses explicit road-topology and lane-connectivity priors. Consequently, the model must recover stable motion cues from short histories while resolving prospective interaction relations without lane-level guidance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a map-free trajectory prediction framework centered on a novel Goal-Conditioned Expert-Routed Transformer (GCERT). A lightweight intra-agent front-end first decomposes projected historical motion features into a smooth trend and a local detail residual through a centered moving average. Component-specific residual projections transform the two signals before a causal temporal Transformer summarizes their recombined evolution. GCERT employs dual-level expert routing: edge-level relation experts generate interaction-specific messages, while node-level state experts adapt the transformation after message aggregation. Predicted motion goals update the node representations and construct prospective relative-geometry and orientation edge features before the final interaction layer, thereby conditioning attention, relation-specific message generation, and state transformation. GCERT therefore determines not only which neighboring agents should be attended to, but also what relation-specific information should be transmitted and how the aggregated node state should be transformed. The resulting representations are decoded into multimodal future trajectories and jointly optimized with trajectory-regression, mode-classification, and goal-prediction objectives.

papers.summary: Deployed AI systems are often trained from broad candidate data pools, necessitating data curation towards the deployment test distribution. However, standard data curation methods score training-side criteria rather than directly optimizing deployment match. We introduce TTCov (Test-Time Coverage), a data-level test-conditioned curation method that uses test-side information before training instead of updating model weights at inference. TTCov decomposes deployment-conditioned curation into coverage and distribution. To represent coverage, it builds a task Atlas, a collection of LLM-based atomic propositions (APs) describing deployment-relevant concepts, seeded from open task knowledge and expanded with unmatched APs extracted from unlabeled deployment samples. To represent distribution, it instantiates the matched deployment APs with their frequencies, yielding a Knowledge Atlas (K-Atlas) that operationalizes the deployment distribution as a curation target. TTCov then selects a budgeted training set whose deployment APs distribution approximates this target. We apply TTCov towards autonomous driving (AD), keeping adaptation off the inference path while selecting data with greater deployment-relevant coverage, closer K-Atlas matching, and stronger downstream end-to-end driving performance than data-curation baselines, including seamless adaptability to novel domains via city-to-city expansion. Code available at https://github.com/NVlabs/TTCov.

papers.title: Classical structural priors improve neural molecular representations in molecule language models
papers.summary: Classical molecular similarity is central to chemical information systems, yet molecule-language models trained on paired structure-text data do not necessarily organize molecular embeddings according to graded structural relationships. Here we introduce Structure-Aware Guided Alignment (SAGA), a training-only regularizer that uses Centered Kernel Alignment to align neural molecular representations with fingerprint-based Tanimoto similarity, without adding parameters or requiring fingerprints at inference. In MolCA and Atomas, SAGA improves molecule-text retrieval, shifts non-exact retrieval toward closer structural analogues, and increases average scaffold-split property-prediction performance, while molecular description and text-to-molecule generation are improved or preserved in single-run ablations. These results show that established chemoinformatics priors can make molecule-language representations more chemically faithful while retaining their multimodal utility.

papers.title: Structure-Guided Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Transformer for Efficient Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation
papers.summary: Existing multi-granularity methods for monocular 3D human pose estimation emphasize spatial joint features while underusing skeletal structure, including global connectivity and temporal continuity. Moreover, modeling entire frame sequences incurs high computational costs. We propose a Structure-Aware Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Transformer that integrates structural priors across spatial and temporal representations for accurate and efficient pose estimation. A three-level feature extractor captures human topology at the joint, bone, and limb levels. Gated Adaptive Spatial Attention (GASA) embeds structural constraints into spatial attention, while Multi-Granularity Feature Enhancement (MGFE) uses hierarchical pooling and fusion to strengthen local details and global semantics. Temporal Segment Fusion (TSF) aligns temporal contexts across granularities to capture both short- and long-range motion patterns. Hierarchical Cross-Attention (HCA) promotes spatiotemporal interaction between granularities, and Keyframe Attention (KFA) selects informative motion segments to reduce redundancy and computational cost. Experiments demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency over conventional Transformer-based approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of structure-aware multi-granularity modeling for monocular 3D human pose estimation.
